assumptions.description: Positive semidefinite, so trace zero implies A = 0.

description_paragraphs: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0$ and $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$; the zero matrix is allowed.
source_fields.description_zh: Assume $A=A^{\mathsf T}\succeq0$ and $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$; the zero matrix is allowed.
source_fields.instance: The unknown input is a real symmetric PSD matrix $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$, including the zero matrix. The target is relative trace error.
source_fields.parameter_domain_description: d>=1, epsilon>0, and 0<delta<1/2; regimes additionally constrain confidence and accuracy windows.

description_paragraphs: The success event is $|\widehat\tau-\tau|\le\varepsilon\tau$. For $\tau>0$ this corresponds to relative loss $|\widehat\tau-\tau|/\tau$; when $\tau=0$, require $\widehat\tau=0$. Positive semidefiniteness ensures $\tau\ge0$.
source_fields.description_zh: The success event is $|\widehat\tau-\tau|\le\varepsilon\tau$. For $\tau>0$ this corresponds to relative loss $|\widehat\tau-\tau|/\tau$; when $\tau=0$, require $\widehat\tau=0$. Positive semidefiniteness ensures $\tau\ge0$.
source_fields.finiteness_conditions: The specified dimension is finite, and the model and spectral assumptions hold.
source_fields.normalization: If both numerator and denominator are zero, the loss is zero. A zero denominator with nonzero numerator gives +∞. Otherwise use the stated ratio.

description_paragraphs: The data $d,\varepsilon,\delta$ are public and $A$ is hidden. Any query $v\in\mathbb{R}^d$ returns exact $Av$. Responses have no sampling noise; randomized probes arise from the algorithm’s private randomness.
source_fields.description_zh: The quantity $d,\varepsilon,\delta$ is public and $A$ is hidden; any $v\in\mathbb R^d$ returns exact $Av$. Responses have no sampling noise. Random probes are choices made using the algorithm's private randomness.

source_fields.allowed_postprocessing: Arbitrary admissible postprocessing; the output need not have appeared as a query vector.
source_fields.certificate_requirement: Only the true-loss guarantee is required; no computable certificate is requested.
description_paragraphs: Return any real $\widehat\tau$, without an additional confidence interval or certificate.
source_fields.description_zh: Return any real $\widehat\tau$, without an additional confidence interval or certificate.

source_fields.budget_semantics: A fixed worst-case budget respected for every input and private seed.

components.description: One right product Av with a single vector

description_paragraphs: Count right products with single vectors only: $N=N_{\mathrm r}$. A block of width $q$ costs $q$ calls.
The budget bounds calls for every fixed input and every private seed. Reading public inputs, exact real arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are free. One call applies the interface to one vector.
source_fields.description_zh:
Count right single-vector products $N=N_{\mathrm{r}}$; a block of width $q$ costs $q$ calls.

The cap holds for every fixed input and private seed. Reading public inputs and exact internal arithmetic, storage, and postprocessing are uncharged. The unit is one single-vector oracle call.
source_fields.precision_model: Inputs, queries, and responses are exact reals. Query vectors have no bit-length restriction. Internal arithmetic, storage, and precision are outside the query budget, so this is not a finite-word implementation guarantee.
source_fields.scalarization: The resource is $Q=N_{\mathrm{right}}$. No separate left-product channel is present. Each block-query column is charged.
source_fields.setup_cost: Reading public parameters and explicitly public $b,x_0,h$, mask, or tree incurs no matrix-vector call. Information about hidden $A$ comes only from native responses.

description_paragraphs: Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.
algorithms.description_zh: Algorithms may use private randomness and choose query vectors adaptively from the declared domain using all previous responses. Queries and outputs may be arbitrary measurable functions of the transcript; no Krylov or linear-span restriction applies. Exact internal arithmetic, storage, and communication are free in this oracle model. A block query is charged by its number of columns.
algorithms.internal_computation: Arbitrary measurable internal computation on public data and the transcript is free in matrix–vector query units. No Krylov or linear-span restriction applies.
algorithms.parallelism: A q-column block still costs q vector products. Round count differs from call count.

guarantees.complete_expression: For each fixed PSD matrix A, require Pr(|t_hat − tr(A)| ≤ ε tr(A)) ≥ 1 − δ. When A = 0, success means outputting exactly zero.
description_paragraphs: The algorithm is selected using public inputs only. For every admissible input fixed before generation of the private seed, success probability over private randomness is at least $1-\delta$.
guarantees.description_zh: The algorithm is selected using public inputs only. For every admissible input fixed before generation of the private seed, success probability over private randomness is at least $1-\delta$.
guarantees.quantifier_order: exists algorithm; forall A PSD; Pr_seed>=1-delta

operations.coupling: Every query accesses the same fixed matrix; repeated queries are allowed.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.index_control: The algorithm selects vectors and an available channel; block width is charged by column.
operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, with only the listed right-product channel available. A q-column block costs q calls. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not free additional feedback.

algorithms.adaptivity: All query vectors are fixed before any response is read.
description_paragraphs: Randomization is allowed, but all query vectors must be chosen at once from public inputs and the private seed. Responses may be used only for final postprocessing and cannot alter the queries. No further span, internal-computation, storage, or communication restriction is imposed; parallel organization does not change per-column charging.
algorithms.description_zh: Randomization is allowed, but all query vectors must be chosen at once from public inputs and the private seed. algorithms.internal_computation: Query vectors are generated jointly before responses. After all responses arrive, arbitrary measurable postprocessing is allowed; internal computation is excluded from matrix-vector cost.
algorithms.parallelism: A q-column block still costs q vector products. Round count differs from call count.

operations.coupling: All vectors depend only on public parameters and the private seed and are chosen jointly before any response.

feedback_quality.description: Exact real vector responses, with no observation noise or rounding.

operations.index_control: Fix every vector before any response. After responses arrive, perform output postprocessing only.
operations.order_convention: Native linear action of the specified matrix; no derivative order of an unregistered scalar function is implied.

oracle.query_domain_description: Right products map R^d to R^d, and only the stated right-product channel is available. A block with q columns costs q queries. Entries, inverse actions, shifted solves, and matrix-function actions are not additional free responses. Every query must be fixed before any response is observed.
